transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I’ve been worrying a lot—probably more than I should. It’s kind of everything at once: my marriage, whether I’m messing up at work, bills, stuff around the house I keep not finishing… and, um, whether I’m failing as a husband and dad. I know that sounds a little dramatic, but it’s been hard to shut off.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or stomach issues along with your worries?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I mean, I haven’t really been tracking it closely. I don’t think there’s anything major like that, or at least nothing I’ve connected clearly to the worrying. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been avoiding any situations or activities because of your worries?

I don’t think so… not in a big obvious way, anyway. I mean, I still go to work and do the usual things. Maybe I put things off sometimes if I’m worried I won’t handle them well, but I’m not sure I’d call it avoiding. Is that what you mean?
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I try not to make it sound worse than it is, but it can get pretty stuck in my head. Like I’ll tell myself, “Just focus on the code in front of you,” or I’ll be working out and trying to breathe through it, and then one worry kind of grabs onto the next one.

It can go from, “What if I get a bad review?” to “What if I lose my job?” to “What if my family is worse off because of me?” And I know that’s jumping way ahead, but in the moment it’s hard to stop it. Is that the kind of repetitive thought you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns since your worries started?

Yeah… I guess my sleep has been kind of affected. I don’t want to overstate it, but most nights I’ll be really tired and then as soon as I’m in bed my mind starts going through things—work risks, money stuff, or something I said to my wife.

Sometimes I do fall asleep, but then I wake up around 3 or 4 and it’s like my brain is already on, rehearsing tomorrow’s problems. Then it’s hard to get back down. Is that the kind of change you’re asking about?
Do you often feel restless or on edge when you're worried?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I still function, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I feel kind of wound tight a lot of the day. Like my shoulders are locked up, and I’m sort of bracing for something even when nothing is happening.

I’ll catch myself pacing between meetings, or if I’m at chess club I’m tapping the pieces or shifting around because sitting still just feels… hard. Is that what you mean by restless or on edge?
Do you often experience muscle tension, like your muscles feeling tight or sore, when you're worried?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m in pain exactly, but I feel kind of wound tight almost all day. My shoulders especially feel locked up, like I’m bracing for something even when there isn’t anything happening.

And I catch myself pacing between meetings, or at chess club I’ll be tapping pieces or shifting around because sitting still feels almost impossible. I’m not sure if that counts as muscle tension the way you mean, but that’s what it feels like.
Have you ever had a sudden, intense feeling of fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?

I don’t think so… not in that really sudden, intense way where it peaks in a few minutes. I mean, I get worked up and uncomfortable, but it’s more like it builds and hangs around rather than hits all at once.

Unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean—does that sound like what you’re asking?
Do you have thoughts that you consider intrusive or unwanted, which you try to suppress or ignore?

Um… not really, I don’t think. I mean, I have worries that repeat in my head, but I don’t know if I’d call them intrusive in the way you mean.

I’m not, like, trying to suppress disturbing thoughts or anything like that. It’s more just… normal worry getting stuck, if that makes sense. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you ever had a period of intense fear or discomfort that included symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve felt stressed and uncomfortable, but I can’t really remember a specific episode where it suddenly got intense with things like my heart racing or not being able to breathe.

Maybe I’m not recognizing it the right way, but I don’t think I’ve had that kind of thing.
Have you ever felt like you were having a heart attack or thought you were going to die when you were worried?

No… I don’t think I’ve ever gotten to the point where I truly thought, “I’m having a heart attack,” or “I’m going to die.”

I can get really worried, and it can feel pretty overwhelming, but not in that kind of immediate, terrifying way. At least, not that I can remember. Does that answer it okay?
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that included physical symptoms like a racing heart or trembling?

I don’t think I’ve had it suddenly like that, no. I mean, I can get really keyed up and tense, but I don’t remember a clear episode where it just hit me all at once with trembling or my heart racing.

If it helps, it feels more like worry building up than a sudden attack. Is that the distinction you mean?
Are your worries usually about a specific situation or problem, or are they more about everything in general?

It’s more… everything in general, I think. I wish it were just one thing I could point to.

I came in because I feel like I can’t stop worrying about a lot of things at once—my marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, house projects I keep dropping… and, honestly, whether I’m kind of failing as a husband and father. I know that may sound dramatic, but that’s where my mind keeps going. Is that the kind of answer you mean?
Are your worries usually about something that's currently happening in your life or are they more about potential future problems?

It’s a bit of both, but I think it leans more toward future “what if” problems. Like, I’m worrying about things that are happening now—my marriage, work, bills, stuff around the house—but my mind turns them into where it’s all going to end up.

Like, am I going to mess things up at work, or fall behind financially, or keep disappointing my family. I don’t want to overstate it, but it feels like everything connects to this fear that I’m not doing enough as a husband or father. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you ever had a sudden episode where you felt an overwhelming fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes and included physical symptoms?

I don’t think so, no. Not in the way you’re describing where it suddenly peaks within a few minutes.

I get anxious, definitely, but it feels more drawn out and kind of… ongoing, rather than one big episode that comes out of nowhere. I hope I’m answering that clearly.
Have your worries been interfering with your ability to enjoy time with your family or perform your job effectively?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say I’m still handling it okay, but it is getting in the way.

At work, my manager has started writing down things I’ve missed—like architectural details I should’ve caught. That’s… embarrassing, because that’s basically my job. And at home, I keep starting projects and not finishing them, or I’m physically there with my family but my head is somewhere else. Then my wife and I end up arguing, and it keeps escalating more than it should.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart, but yes, it’s definitely affecting both. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever experienced a discrete episode of intense fear that reached a peak within minutes?

I don’t think I have, no. I mean, I get really anxious, but I wouldn’t describe it as a separate episode that suddenly peaks within minutes. It’s more like it builds or just stays with me.

If there’s a specific kind of episode you mean, I can try to think about it more.
Would you say that your worries are causing you significant distress or are getting in the way of your daily life and relationships?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s definitely been affecting things.

At work, my manager has started documenting architectural details I’ve missed, which feels pretty bad because that’s a big part of what I’m supposed to catch. And at home, I’ll start projects and then leave them half-finished, or I’m there but distracted, and then my wife and I end up arguing more than we should.

So… yeah, I’d say it’s getting in the way. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Are your worries usually centered around one main fear or concern, or are they more scattered across different areas of your life?

It’s more scattered, I think. I wish it were just one thing, because maybe that would feel more manageable, but it’s kind of… everything at once.

I worry about my marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, the house projects I keep not finishing… and then it turns into this bigger worry that I’m failing as a husband or a father. I know that probably sounds dramatic, and I’m not trying to make it sound worse than it is, but that’s honestly how it feels some days.
Do you find that your worries follow you into most areas of your life, such as work, home, and social situations?

Yes… it does. I mean, I try not to let it spill into everything, but it kind of does.

That’s honestly part of why I came in. I feel like I can’t stop worrying about everything at once—my marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, the house projects I keep dropping… and then it turns into this worry that I’m basically failing as a husband and father.

I know that probably sounds like a lot, but it’s not really staying in one lane, if that makes sense.
